item.title: MPs had no time to properly scrutinise Constitution Amendment Bill – Chaudhry
item.description: Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry has questioned the legitimacy of the Constitution amendment process, claiming it was rushed and MPs were not given enough time to properly read, analyse and debate the Bill. Chaudhry questioned why there was a need to rush the process after what he says was little action on constitutional reform during the Government’s three and a half years in office.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry has questioned the legitimacy of the Constitution amendment process, claiming it was rushed and MPs were not given enough time to properly read, analyse and debate the Bill.

Chaudhry questioned why there was a need to rush the process after what he says was little action on constitutional reform during the Government’s three and a half years in office.

He claims there must be an agenda behind the rushed process and says the Government made several mistakes in its haste.

Chaudhry also claims the Government treated the Supreme Court opinion as law without presenting a Bill to Parliament to convert the opinion into law.

He says they have challenged the legitimacy of the process from the beginning and intend to continue raising the matter as the process moves forward.

Chaudhry also criticised NFP Leader Professor Biman Prasad for supporting the Constitution Amendment Bill.

He referred to Prasad’s comments on 18th September that the NFP would not be part of any attempt to rush the implementation of a new Constitution, and described his subsequent support for the Bill as a turnaround.

Chaudhry says 38 MPs supported the Bill and claims Prasad’s support gave the Government the numbers it needed.

He also raised concerns about the amount of time MPs had to consider the Bill, saying the report was given to them late on Wednesday afternoon before Parliament sat throughout Thursday and into early Friday morning.

Chaudhry questioned when MPs had time to read, analyse and understand the Bill before it was tabled on Friday morning, saying it would have been impossible to have a meaningful debate in that timeframe.

He claims the lack of time for a full debate raises questions about the validity of the process.

The Bill has now been referred to a bipartisan parliamentary committee for 30 days to seek public views and prepare a report before the third reading.

Chaudhry says attention should also turn to the next general election, which he says Parliament has been told will be held before 6th February 2027 under the 2013 Constitution.

item.title: I was not good academically, but my father taught me the value of hard work – Serevi
item.description: Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Serevi opened up about his life before the trophies and international success, saying he grew up in Nasole in a family of five children. Serevi says he has an older brother and sister and a younger brother and sister, making him the middle child, who he jokingly describes as the peacekeeper in the family.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking on fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, Serevi opened up about his life before the trophies and international success, saying he grew up in Nasole in a family of five children.

Serevi says he has an older brother and sister and a younger brother and sister, making him the middle child, who he jokingly describes as the peacekeeper in the family.

He says growing up was challenging, but the difficulties he faced taught him many important lessons.

Speaking about his education, Serevi says he attended Delainamasi Government School from Class 1 to Class 6, but school was always difficult for him.

He says he did not pass his Class 8 examination but was able to continue his education at Lelean Memorial School after his father approached pastors he knew and asked if Serevi could continue to Form 3.

Serevi attended Lelean Memorial School from 1980 to 1984 before his school journey ended after he failed his Fiji Junior Certificate Examination.

Insert: Serevi on working hard 4th Oct 26

Serevi says that lesson taught him the importance of working hard before enjoying the rewards.

He says he now shares the same message with school children, reminding them that they do not need to have a paid job to learn the value of work.

Serevi says simple responsibilities such as making their bed, picking up rubbish, doing the laundry and washing dishes before going to school can help young people develop discipline.

He says the hardworking attitude that followed him throughout his life came from those early lessons taught by his father.

item.title: Kartik Naidu pursues Eskrima martial arts journey from Fiji to the Philippines
item.description: 29-year-old Fijian martial artist Kartik Naidu has travelled to Cebu City in the Philippines to further his training in San Miguel Eskrima and learn directly under Supreme Grandmaster Panto Canete Flores. Naidu who is a Police officer and Pastor began learning San Miguel Eskrima several months ago under the guidance of one of Flores top students.
item.content:encoded:
29-year-old Fijian martial artist Kartik Naidu has travelled to Cebu City in the Philippines to further his training in San Miguel Eskrima and learn directly under Supreme Grandmaster Panto Canete Flores.

Naidu who is a Police officer and Pastor began learning San Miguel Eskrima several months ago under the guidance of one of Flores top students.

Flores says Naidu's love, passion and commitment to martial arts led him to travel from Fiji to the Philippines to meet him personally and continue his training face-to-face.

He says Naidu's goal is to deepen his knowledge, strengthen his techniques and further develop his skills as he works towards the Master Level of Filipino Martial Arts.

Flores says throughout his journey, Naidu remains committed to honouring the principles, traditions and legacy of San Miguel Eskrima.

Naidu also has a background in boxing, having trained in Fiji under the guidance of his father, George Tavuna.

Flores says their training helped Naidu develop practical fighting techniques, discipline and valuable martial arts experience.

He says Naidu's journey reflects his dedication to learning, respect for martial arts and determination to expand his knowledge and skills through direct training and guidance.

item.title: Blocked Nanuku Creek raises health concerns as wastewater flows into Rifle Range drains
item.description: Dark, foul-smelling wastewater flowing into residential drains is raising health concerns among Rifle Range residents in Vatuwaqa, who say the nearby Nanuku Creek has not been dredged since 2022. Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirmal Singh says the problem has been ongoing for the past three years.
item.content:encoded:
Dark, foul-smelling wastewater flowing into residential drains is raising health concerns among Rifle Range residents in Vatuwaqa, who say the nearby Nanuku Creek has not been dredged since 2022.

Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirmal Singh says the problem has been ongoing for the past three years.

Singh says the mouth of the creek is blocked by accumulated rubbish and silt, causing wastewater to flow into the residential drainage system.

He says a foul smell coming from the creek makes it difficult for residents living nearby to sleep with their windows open.

Singh says he has personally visited the Suva City Council several times and spoken with the Administrator and engineering and health staff about the concerns faced by Rifle Range residents.

He says Council staff had indicated that an inspection would be carried out and the creek dredged, but there has been no progress.

Insert: Singh on what the Council is doing, 4th Oct

Singh says raw sewage can also leak into the creek when sewerage pumps are not working.

He says children from the nearby Nanuku settlement have at times been seen fishing in the creek, raising concerns about their exposure to the polluted water.

Singh says residents expect the Council to address the drainage and creek issues and hopes their concerns will now be taken seriously.

We have sent questions to the Suva City Council.
